scholarships.name: Samia Scholarship
scholarships.sponsor: Government of Tanzania (Ministry of Education, run with HESLB)
scholarships.eligibility: Top 2026 ACSEE (Form Six) performers in science combinations: PCB, PCM, CBG, PGM, CBA, PMC or CBN. About 1,000 places.
scholarships.covers: Study in STEM (science, technology, engineering and mathematics) programmes at Tanzanian universities. Check the HESLB guidelines for exactly what is paid.
scholarships.timing: Opens after ACSEE results (2026 window opened 28 July 2026). Students are selected on results, then confirm online.
scholarships.how_to_apply: Apply through HESLB's online system (OLAMS/OLAS) once the Ministry of Education publishes the list of eligible students.

scholarships.name: Samia Scholarship Extended (DS/AI+)
scholarships.eligibility: About 50 students with exceptional ACSEE results in Physics and Advanced Mathematics.
scholarships.covers: Data science and artificial intelligence studies at IIT Madras Zanzibar.
scholarships.timing: Opens with the main Samia Scholarship after ACSEE results (late July).
scholarships.how_to_apply: Apply through the Ministry of Education's TEMIS portal (temis.moe.go.tz).

scholarships.name: HESLB Student Loan
scholarships.status: 2026/27 window closed · next opens about June 2027
scholarships.eligibility: Tanzanian students admitted to bachelor's (and some diploma) programmes who need financial help. About 280,000 students funded in 2026/27 (TZS 1.07 trillion).
scholarships.covers: Can cover tuition, meals and accommodation, books and stationery, field practicals and special faculty needs, depending on the student's need.
scholarships.timing: Usually opens in June and runs about 2–3 months (2026/27 window opened 19 June 2026).
scholarships.how_to_apply: Apply online through OLAMS. One-off, non-refundable application fee of TZS 30,000.

scholarships.name: Mwalimu Julius K. Nyerere Memorial Scholarship Fund
scholarships.status: No 2026 advert on the BoT page right now · watch for July 2027
scholarships.eligibility: Tanzanians who just finished ACSEE with Division One. Category A: women in science or mathematics. Category B: men and women in science, mathematics, IT, economics, accounting or finance.
scholarships.covers: Full scholarship: tuition and direct university costs, meals and accommodation, books and stationery, field practicals, plus a new laptop.
scholarships.timing: Usually advertised in late July with an August deadline (2025 deadline: 22 August 2025).
scholarships.how_to_apply: Download the form from the BoT website (or collect it at a BoT office), fill it in, scan it and email it to the Fund chairperson. Only shortlisted candidates are contacted.

scholarships.name: NMB Nuru Yangu Scholarship
scholarships.status: Announced Sept 2026 · check whether still open
scholarships.eligibility: Form Six leavers from low-income families with excellent results. For 2026, NMB set aside TZS 1 billion for students with Division One (3–5 points).
scholarships.covers: Full tuition, stipend, field allowance, stationery and a laptop, all direct university costs, and a mentorship programme.
scholarships.how_to_apply: Register a profile on the NMB Foundation website, complete the form and attach certified PDF copies of documents. Only shortlisted candidates are contacted.

scholarships.name: Mo Scholars Program
scholarships.status: 2026 window closed · next round about Sept 2027
scholarships.eligibility: Tanzanians aged 18–25 entering the first year of a bachelor's degree, with Division One at A-level (or diploma GPA 4.0+), admission to a recognised institution, financial need and community leadership.
scholarships.covers: Full tuition, accommodation, meals, study materials including a laptop, mentorship, leadership training and the alumni network. Any field. Renewable each year.
scholarships.how_to_apply: Apply online on the Foundation's portal with transcripts, admission letter, NIDA number or birth certificate, proof of need (e.g. TASAF or local government letter) and a photo.

scholarships.name: Karimjee Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.eligibility: Tanzanian citizens schooled in Tanzania with Division One (or GPA 3.6+) at O-level and A-level, admitted to a bachelor's or diploma programme in Tanzania, with critical financial need. Priority for girls and students with disabilities.
scholarships.covers: Support for undergraduate or diploma study in Tanzania (amount not published). Recipients report results every semester.
scholarships.timing: No fixed deadline published. Selection includes an exam and interview.
scholarships.how_to_apply: Register at scholarship.karimjee.com; shortlisted students complete a full application (essay, letter, admission letter, fee structure, transcripts, CV, HESLB status). Contact: foundation@karimjee.com, +255 222 112 986.

scholarships.name: Flaviana Matata Foundation
scholarships.eligibility: Girls from underserved communities. FMF supports students from secondary school through college.
scholarships.how_to_apply: No online form. Contact FMF at TGB Building, Coca-Cola Rd, Mikocheni, Dar es Salaam, or through the contact page on its website.

scholarships.name: AfricAid University Scholarships
scholarships.eligibility: Young women who graduated from AfricAid's Kisa leadership programme in Tanzanian secondary schools.
scholarships.covers: University study for selected Kisa graduates (amount not published).
scholarships.how_to_apply: Ask your school's Kisa programme coordinator.
